A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HyPER work. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, dense-model and tree-search experiments, and an expert-routing simulation.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments and adds dataset-level confidence analysis and hardware profiling.

M1.justification: The controller, action library, two-pass expert sampler, cache sharing and voting procedure remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1 and 2. The newly specified voting cutoff is an implementation disclosure; the dense-model adaptation already appeared in v1.

E1.justification: v2 removes the synthetic 16-expert routing environment evaluated in v1 Appendix F.3 and Figure 15. Reasoning benchmarks and task coverage remain unchanged; the new confidence analysis and profiling use existing benchmarks.

E2.justification: The independent-routing RoE comparison against the penalty scheme labelled ProE disappears with v1 Figure 15. SC, Self-Certainty, DeepConf and RoE remain in the main comparisons, and the dense-model, ablation and tree-search comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix I introduces a substantial systems-evaluation extension: raw and effective tokens, latency, concurrent-path statistics and estimated KV memory on identical A100-80GB hardware. Figure 2 introduces length-normalized confidence analysis across questions. Existing benchmark budgets and settings are largely retained; these additions do not establish reruns of the main experiments.

E4.justification: Figure 2 replaces an individual reasoning example with dataset-level evidence about late confidence divergence. Appendix I adds analysis of physical execution overhead, while the routing-diversity simulation is removed. Existing sensitivity, voting, length-bias, dense-model and tree-search analyses remain.

E5.justification: The explicit Monte Carlo averaging over random router realizations reported for v1 Figure 15 disappears with that simulation. Table 2 retains identical uncertainty entries, and v2 adds no run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2-7 retain their numerical results. New Table 8 adds substantial execution-cost results; for example, Qwen3-30B/HMMT25 HyPER has reported latency of 8.38 million ms and estimated peak KV memory of 28.4 GB. Figure 2 supplies new aggregate confidence curves, while the earlier routing-simulation results disappear.

T1.justification: v2 removes the existence-selection inequality and majority-vote counterexample from Appendix F.1, plus Appendix F.3's collision-reduction proposition, proof and marginal-routing expansion. The importance-sampling interpretation, propositions and voting derivation from v1 Appendix F.2 survive as v2 Appendix F.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions and claims about adaptive exploration, token refinement, answer selection and dense-model applicability remain. The abstract and introduction retain the same claimed accuracy gains and token savings; Figure 2 changes supporting evidence rather than the central claim.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly argues that raw-token savings translate into latency and memory benefits that offset controller and routing overhead. Section 4.1 replaces v1's assertion of identical token consumption with effective-path-budget accounting. The removed routing analysis also removes its interpretation of small marginal-distribution perturbations.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the answer-voting cutoff Ka=3 and A100-80GB profiling hardware, and explains the additional accounting metrics. It removes the HLE 'all multi-answer questions' qualifier and examples of warm-up normalization sources, without establishing changed data or procedures. Algorithms and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds Wang et al.'s 'Every rollout counts: Optimal resource allocation for efficient test-time scaling.' Most other reference edits correct metadata or consolidate the duplicate inference-scaling citation. The paper's substantive positioning against existing reasoning methods remains stable.

P1.justification: Observation 2 and Sections 4.1-4.2 receive localized rewrites. The appendices reorganize retained theory and experiments and add Appendix I. Publication and correspondence information change, while most prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes an aggregate confidence plot, Figures 14-15 disappear, and Table 8 is added. Figure 4 and Tables 2-3 are enlarged, while Figure 6 and Table 4 move. These are targeted display and placement changes within the retained document design.

improvement.justification: Dataset-level Figure 2 strengthens the empirical motivation beyond v1's individual example, while Appendix I adds practical efficiency evidence beyond normalized token costs. Specifying Ka=3 also improves reproducibility. These gains are limited by reduced theoretical support and incomplete profiling explanations, including how Table 8's HyPER peak path counts above 80 relate to the stated default cap.
